job_summary: Commercial tenant improvement in Savannah, GA converting a former 2,200 sq ft retail space into a full-service restaurant. Scope triggers a Building Permit for the interior alteration/change of use, plus trade permits for plumbing, mechanical, electrical, and Because this is a commercial renovation, Savannah also requires the commercial renovation application package and Water & Sewer Planning/Engineering sign-off before Building Permit issuance.

permits_required_logic.permit_type: Building Permit — Tenant Improvement / Restaurant Interior Alteration
permits_required_logic.included_because: Commercial TI/change-of-use scopes must lead with a building/interior-alteration permit; trade permits are companion permits unless the job is only a trade changeout.
Commercial HVAC, ventilation, exhaust, diffuser/RTU, or air-balance scope is stated and commonly requires mechanical review.
Commercial lighting, panels, branch circuits, equipment, emergency lighting, controls, or low-voltage/electrical scope is stated and commonly requires electrical review.
Commercial kitchen fixtures, grease-interceptor/FOG work, restrooms, sinks, and DWV changes commonly require plumbing review.

approval_timeline.simple: Commercial TI/addition/remodel scopes usually require plan review; expect at least several business days to a few weeks depending on completeness, valuation, and local queue.
approval_timeline.complex: 1-3 weeks for commercial plan review, longer if Water & Sewer sign-off, Fire Marshal review, or historic district review is required.

inspections.description: Inspector checks demo limits, new partition layout, fire-resistance ratings where required, door swings/egress, accessibility clearances, and that no structural members were altered without approval.
inspections.timing: After framing and layout are complete, before drywall or ceiling closure

inspections.description: Inspector verifies grease interceptor location and sizing, floor drain placement and slope, restroom fixture rough-ins, venting, trap arms, cleanouts, and that the three-compartment sink is properly drained and vented.
inspections.timing: Before slab patching, insulation, or wall/ceiling closure

inspections.description: Inspector verifies panel upgrade installation, feeder sizing, breaker labeling, dedicated cooking equipment circuits, GFCI/AFCI where applicable, equipment disconnects, grounding/bonding, and working clearances at the panel.

inspection_booking: Schedule inspections through Savannah Development Services / eTRAC using the city permit portal. Phone: (912) 651-6790. For commercial work, book inspections with at least 24 hours advance notice; if you need after-hours inspection, Savannah lists a $260 fee for 4 hours plus $65/hour. Have the permit number, address, contractor name, and requested inspection type ready when scheduling.
what_to_bring: Completed commercial renovation application package for the Building Permit
Signed Water & Sewer Planning and Engineering approval form for the commercial renovation application
Scaled floor plan showing demo, new partitions, kitchen layout, restroom layout, and equipment locations
Contractor license numbers and business information for GC, plumbing, mechanical, electrical, and fire protection trades
Project valuation breakdown for building, plumbing, mechanical, electrical, and fire protection scope
common_mistakes: Submitting the commercial building permit application without the Water & Sewer Planning and Engineering signed approval form — Savannah will not accept the renovation application without it.
Trying to pull the whole restaurant build-out under only a building permit — the plumbing, mechanical, electrical, and fire protection scopes still need their own trade permits.
Understating project valuation to reduce fees — Savannah uses valuation-based fees and can reprice the permit if the declared value is unrealistic.
Submitting permit applications without verifying current contractor license status — an expired or lapsed license will block the application and delay review.
pro_tips: Get the Water & Sewer Planning and Engineering sign-off first; that is the Savannah-specific gate that most often delays restaurant TI permits.
Bundle the building, plumbing, mechanical, electrical, and fire protection submittals with one coordinated plan set so plan review does not bounce the job between departments.
Use a realistic valuation on the permit application — Savannah's building fee is $8 per $1,000, so a clean, accurate valuation avoids correction cycles.
If the project is in or near the Historic District, check for Historic District Board review before you submit; that can add time even for interior renovation work.
Verify contractor registration and license expiration dates before opening the portal — a lapsed credential is one of the fastest ways to get a commercial permit rejected.

companion_permits.reason: Restaurant scopes with food-prep, kitchen, bar, sink, dishwashing, or opening work commonly require health review before opening.
Commercial kitchen plumbing often requires grease interceptor/FOG approval.
Commercial tenant improvements commonly trigger accessible route, restroom, door/hardware, counter, parking, or 20% disproportionality review.

zoning_hoa_flag: Historic District review may apply in Savannah depending on the property location. For a restaurant conversion, also verify zoning use approval, parking/loading requirements, grease interceptor sizing, and any downtown/historic overlay restrictions before finalizing the tenant improvement plans.
